provenanceRule: Groups are editorial retrieval labels, not IB syllabus headings. Every group names its complete official item membership explicitly; membership is one-to-one across this file.
groupingPrinciples: Group adjacent official items only when students would reasonably study and search for them together.
Keep operation boundaries explicit so neighboring groups are mutually exclusive for primary classification.
Preserve official teaching order within each parent topic; group order follows the course topic order.
Applicability is the union of member item applicability: SL content is available to SL and HL; HL-only content is HL.

groups.studentFacingName: Standard form and orders of magnitude

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Writing and interpreting numbers as a × 10^k with 1 ≤ a < 10.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Calculator notation, significant figures, or ordinary place value when standard form is not the assessed object.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Arithmetic/geometric nth terms and sums, compound growth, depreciation, inflation and related financial models.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Infinite-series convergence (1.8), or finance word problems that do not use a sequence/series model.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Integer/rational exponent laws, introductory logarithms, logarithm laws, change of base and solving exponential equations with logarithms.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Graphing exponential/logarithmic functions (2.9), or a merely numerical logarithm evaluation with no exponent/log law focus.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Elementary deduction plus HL induction, contradiction and counterexamples.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: A proof incidental to another mathematical task, or verification by examples without a proof-method objective.

groups.studentFacingName: Infinite series and the binomial theorem

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Convergence and sums of infinite geometric series, natural-index binomial expansion and binomial coefficients.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Finite geometric sums (1.3), counting/fractional-index extensions (1.10), or unrelated polynomial expansion.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Permutations, combinations, and binomial expansion for fractional or negative indices.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Natural-index binomial expansion (1.9), or circular/identical-object counting outside the stated scope.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Decomposing rational expressions into the guide-specified partial fractions.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Routine factorization or simplification that does not require partial-fraction decomposition.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Cartesian and polar/Argand representations, modulus/argument, roots, De Moivre and complex-number operations.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Real-number algebra, or a complex expression where complex representation is incidental and not assessed.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Solving and interpreting systems up to three linear equations in three unknowns.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: A single linear equation or a nonlinear system.

groups.studentFacingName: Straight lines, functions, domain and range

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Line equations/gradients and the function concept, notation, domain, range and informal inverse idea.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Reading graph features as the main task (2.3–2.4), or composite/inverse manipulation (2.5).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Reading/drawing y=f(x) and identifying intercepts, extrema, symmetry, asymptotes and other key features.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: A deliberate graph transformation (2.11/2.16), or solving an equation as the primary objective (2.10).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Composition, identity and inverse functions, including one-to-one conditions and composition identities.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: HL inverse-function properties with restrictions/self-inverse functions (2.14), or graph transformations.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Quadratic forms and graphs, roots, formula, parameters, equations and inequalities.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Higher-degree polynomial work (2.12), or a quadratic appearing only as an incidental algebraic step.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Reciprocal/linear-over-linear graphs and HL rational functions, including asymptotes, intercepts and related features.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: A polynomial function (2.12), or a reciprocal expression used only as an algebraic fraction.

groups.studentFacingName: Exponential and logarithmic functions and equations

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Graphs and inverse relationship of exponential/logarithmic functions, plus graphical or analytic equation solving.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Exponent/log laws without function graphs/equations (1.5/1.7).

groups.studentFacingName: Transformations of functions and modulus graphs

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Translations, stretches, reflections, modulus constructions and the specified f(ax+b), 1/f(x) and [f(x)]² transformations.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Simple graph reading (2.3–2.4) or solving a standalone modulus equation without graph transformation as the main idea.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL polynomial graphs, roots, factors and equations beyond the dedicated quadratic treatment.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Quadratics handled entirely within 2.6–2.7.

groups.studentFacingName: Function symmetry, periodicity and restricted inverses

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL odd/even and periodic functions, domain-restricted inverses and self-inverse functions.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Basic inverse/composite procedures (2.5) or trigonometric symmetry (3.11).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL solving and interpreting g(x) ≥ f(x) graphically or analytically.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Single-function quadratic inequalities (2.7) or modulus inequalities when no function comparison is involved.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: SL/HL distance, midpoint, volume, surface area and restricted angles between lines/planes in 3D.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Vector line/plane algebra (3.12 onward).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Right-triangle ratios, sine/cosine rules, area formula, Pythagoras, bearings, elevation/depression and triangle applications.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Unit-circle identities/equations or circular-function graphs as the main operation.

groups.studentFacingName: Radians, arc length and sector area

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Radian measure and calculations of arc length or sector area.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Circular-function graphing or equation solving where radians are merely the unit.

groups.studentFacingName: Unit-circle definitions and exact trigonometric values

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Unit-circle definitions/relationships, exact sine/cosine/tangent values and the ambiguous sine-rule case.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Identity proof/manipulation (3.6), or solving a trigonometric equation (3.8).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Pythagorean, double-angle and related sine/cosine identity simplification or proof.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Compound-angle identities and tan double-angle at HL (3.10), or equation solving (3.8).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Graphs, amplitude, period, transformations and real-life models using sin, cos and tan.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Solving trig equations (3.8), reciprocal/inverse functions (3.9), or pure identity manipulation (3.6).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Graphical and analytic solutions of trigonometric equations over a stated finite interval.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Proving/simplifying identities or drawing a graph without solving an equation.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL sec, cosec, cot and inverse trigonometric functions, including domains, ranges, identities and graphs.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Basic sin/cos/tan graphing (3.7) or compound-angle identities (3.10).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL compound-angle identities and the double-angle identity for tan.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: The SL identity set (3.6) when no compound-angle operation is assessed.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL relationships among trigonometric functions and symmetry properties of their graphs.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Basic circular graphs (3.7) or general function symmetry unrelated to trigonometry (2.14).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL 2D/3D vectors, position/displacement, scalar product and angles between vectors.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Vector product (3.16) or equations of lines/planes (3.14/3.17).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL vector equations, relationships among lines, vector product, planes, intersections and angles of lines/planes.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Non-vector 3D measurement (3.1) or scalar-product-only work (3.13).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Population/sample ideas, data quality, bias, outliers, sampling methods, frequency tables and appropriate displays.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Calculating summary statistics (4.3) or modelling probability distributions.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Mean, median, mode, grouped estimates, quartiles, IQR, variance, standard deviation and effects of linear changes.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Correlation/regression (4.4/4.10) or distribution probabilities.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Scatter plots, Pearson correlation, lines of best fit, both stated regression directions and prediction.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Causal claims, non-linear regression, or descriptive statistics without a bivariate relationship.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Sample spaces, events, complements, expected occurrences, Venn/tree diagrams, combined/conditional/independent probabilities and replacement.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Bayes reversal as the named method (4.13), or random-variable distribution calculations (4.7 onward).

groups.studentFacingName: Discrete random variables and binomial distribution

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Discrete probability distributions, expected value and the binomial model including mean and variance.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Continuous variables/densities (4.14) or normal modelling (4.9/4.12).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Normal curves, properties, z-standardization and probabilities/values from the standard normal variable.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Non-normal discrete models or regression.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Formal conditional probability and HL Bayes’ theorem, including reversal across the stated event scope.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Simple conditional probability with no Bayes reversal may still be 4.11; do not use this group for independence alone.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL continuous variables, density functions, mode/median/mean, variance, standard deviation, transformations and fair games; includes discrete moments where assessed in this HL item.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Normal distribution specifically (4.9/4.12) or basic discrete distributions (4.7/4.8).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Informal limits, derivative as gradient/rate of change, and using derivative sign to identify increasing/decreasing intervals.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Formal HL limit evaluation (5.12/5.13) or routine differentiation rules (5.3/5.6).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Power and standard-function derivatives, chain/product/quotient rules, and tangent or normal equations.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Derivative-sign analysis (5.2) or optimization/concavity as the primary objective (5.7–5.8).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Second derivative and concavity, extrema, inflection, optimization, displacement/velocity/acceleration and total distance.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: A derivative calculation with no application, or integration-based area/kinematics.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: Antidifferentiation, standard integrals, substitution in the stated form, definite integrals and areas between curves.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: HL integration by parts/advanced methods (5.16), volumes of revolution (5.17), or differential equations.

groups.studentFacingName: Continuity, higher derivatives and evaluated limits

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL continuity/differentiability, first-principles and higher derivatives, convergence/divergence and evaluated limits using l’Hôpital or Maclaurin.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Informal SL limits (5.1) or ordinary derivative rules without HL limit reasoning.

groups.studentFacingName: Implicit differentiation, related rates and advanced optimization

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL implicit differentiation, related rates and optimization including endpoint optima.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Explicit-function optimization already covered by 5.8, or routine related-rate arithmetic with no implicit/HL method.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL derivatives and antiderivatives involving tan, sec, cosec, cot, exponential/logarithmic and inverse-trigonometric functions, including partial fractions.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Basic standard-function differentiation/integration (5.6/5.10) when no extended function or method is central.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL integration by substitution and integration by parts, including repeated parts.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: The elementary substitution form in 5.10 or an antiderivative requiring no named method.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL area bounded by a curve and the y-axis and volumes generated by rotation about the x- or y-axis.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Plane area between curves without revolution (5.11).

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL Euler’s method and separable, homogeneous or linear first-order differential equations with integrating factor.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: A generic sequence/recurrence or a higher-order differential equation outside the stated scope.

classificationBoundary.inclusive: HL Maclaurin expansions and deriving further series by substitution, products, differentiation/integration, with approximations.
classificationBoundary.exclusive: Infinite geometric series (1.8) or a limit using a series where no Maclaurin expansion is the assessed method.
